title: Quarterly Rally: Facilitation Notes & Exec Prep (Q3 2026 Draft)
content:
Purpose:
- Create a compact, rehearsal-ready facilitation plan for the company-wide Q3 Rally (one-hour live + 30m breakout + 15m open mic). This doc is the working instrument for execs, comms, and ops.

Audience:
- Full company (~150). Emphasis on engineers, product, and customer-facing teams.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
1) Shared clarity on top 3 company commitments for the quarter (one-liners + why they matter).
2) Visible alignment between OKR drafts and product/eng roadmaps (no surprises).
3) Actionable asks for ICs and managers (clear owners & 30/60/90-day checkpoints).
4) Two-way signal: sense-checks from staff via live poll and 3 breakout prompts.

Why this matters (narrative to open):
- We are moving from early growth into predictable serving scale. This quarter is about converting platform investments into measurable inference economics improvements (latency, cost, reliability) while keeping developer experience fast. Reinforce the thesis: serving > model hoarding.

Top-line commitments (draft OKR framing):
- Objective A: Reduce median tail latency for hosted API across common sequences by 25% (SLO alignment + two fallbacks).
  - Key Result A1: Move 80% of production traffic onto the new kernel-selection runtime by end of Q3.
  - Key Result A2: P95 latency < 180ms for 1k token seqs for tier-1 models.

- Objective B: Improve unit economics for text generation workloads by 20% (tokens-per-dollar).
  - Key Result B1: Deploy prefix/KV caching enhancements to 3 highest-volume customers and measure 10% per-token savings.
  - Key Result B2: Ship optimized quantization profiles for two model families and validate quality regressions < 1% on eval set.

- Objective C: Mature Private offerings (VPC & on-prem) to enterprise readiness.
  - Key Result C1: Complete SOC-2 readiness checklist + KMS integration for first pilot customer.
  - Key Result C2: Launch private-region beta with one major customer and document operational playbook.

Notes on framing (language for execs):
- Avoid deep technical jargon in the main narrative (save for breakout rooms). Use one-sentence analogies: e.g., "We are tuning how requests flow so your app sees faster replies and lower bills."
- Spotlight customer outcomes (latency improvements = fewer user cancellations, cost improvements = fewer price-sensitive throttles).

Run of show (60m main + 30m breakouts + 15m open mic):
1) 0:00 - 0:05  - Welcome & context (CEO) — 1 sentence on mission and why this quarter matters.
2) 0:05 - 0:15  - State of the Product (CTO) — 3 bullets: performance, cost, private deployments. Call out top metric shifts since last quarter.
3) 0:15 - 0:25  - OKR snapshot (Head of Product) — show objectives and lead measures; ask: "Which KR do we need to double-down on?"
4) 0:25 - 0:35  - Customer vignette (CS) — short case: how Dedicated reduced latency for X customer (concrete numbers).
5) 0:35 - 0:45  - People & org ask (People Ops) — hiring focus, role priorities, how to apply for rotation programs.
6) 0:45 - 0:55  - Engineering deep-dive (serving runtime lead) — two-min demo clip (video) + risk-mitigation plan.
7) 0:55 - 1:00  - Close & ask (CEO) — three clear asks for team.
8) 1:00 - 1:30  - Breakouts (pre-assigned) — 5 groups by theme (performance, cost & billing, private deployments, console/observability, customer ops).
9) 1:30 - 1:45  - Open mic + prioritized live Q&A (execs filter).

Facilitator script highlights (bullets to read):
- "We have three bets this quarter — speed, cost, and private readiness. Each team will have a role in one of those bets."
- Always reframe answers to the "why it matters" level.
- During breakout time: ask groups to surface 1 risk + 1 tangible owner + 1 quick win we can do in 30 days.

Breakout prompts (deliverable = 1 slide summary per group):
- Performance group: Identify a single end-to-end stack change that reduces our P95 by at least 10% for a major workload.
- Cost group: Propose a small config change in batching/caching that yields >= 5% token-cost reduction for a test cohort.
- Private group: List the top 3 operational gaps preventing pilot readiness and a stopgap for each.
- Console group: Name two dashboards we need in 2 weeks to signal regressions.
- Customer ops: Suggest one playbook for Tier-1 incidents that reduces MTTR by 15%.

Polling & measurement (live during main session):
- Quick poll: "Which KR feels most at risk?" (single choice)
- Follow-up free text: "One thing you need leadership to unblock this quarter" (short answers)
- Use Slido/Polls; collect results and synthesize in #rally-summary

Exec prep Q&A (FAQ style snippets for CEO/CTO):
- Q: "What if a major quantization causes quality regressions?"
  A: "Pause rollout, revert to compatible variant, run the eval suite and threshold gating; customer-impact playbook in GitHub PR link."
- Q: "How will we communicate outages to customers?"
  A: "Tiered communications: Dedicated customers get an incident runbook and a named AE. Hosted customers get status page + postmortem commit."

Risk register (top 6 unmitigated risks):
1) Kernel selection rollout causes unexpected regressions at scale. Owner: runtime eng lead. Mitigation: phased traffic shifting + automatic rollback.
2) Cache/ batching changes degrade latency in tail cases. Owner: performance squad. Mitigation: A/B traffic split + synthetic load tests.
3) Private pilot delays due to KMS integration. Owner: private infra eng. Mitigation: early sandbox KMS + contract clause for customer pilots.
4) Hiring lag for SRE/infra roles. Owner: People Ops + Eng hiring leads. Mitigation: prioritize contractor runway + intern conversions.
5) Misalignment on OKRs between product and sales (overpromising capabilities). Owner: product ops. Mitigation: weekly sync + acceptance criteria gating.
6) Communication fatigue (too many meetings). Owner: company-ops. Mitigation: concise comms, pre-read + 1-pager recaps.

Logistics checklist (ops to check before live):
- Room & AV test (video clip ready) — Marco
- Slide deck consolidated and under 20 slides — Priya
- Rehearsal with execs (run-through) — Friday 9am — Ava
- Polls created and tested in Slido — Sofia
- Breakout facilitators briefed and templates uploaded — Liam
- Live captioning & recording scheduled — People Ops

Rehearsal plan (this week):
- Tue: Tech check with AV (10m).
- Wed: Walkthrough with speakers only (30m) — focus on transitions.
- Thu: Full dress (30m) with facilitators + Q&A gating.
- Friday: Final sign-off with CEO (15m).

Open issues / decisions needed (short):
- Decision: Accept the three-objective framing above? (Due: Wed EOD)
- Question: Which two KRs require external vendor support (procurement lead)?
- Ask: Product to provide 2x slide-level metrics (latency trend, cost per 1M tokens) by Thu morning.

Post-rally artifacts (owner & timeline):
- 1-pager recap + action owners (company-ops, by +48h)
- Consolidated breakout slide deck (facilitators, +72h)
- OKR finalization meeting invites (product ops, +1 week)
- Public-facing summary for customers (marketing + CS, +1 week)

Tone & communication tips for presenters:
- Be candid about trade-offs. If something slipped, say why and what we learned.
- Use one metric to anchor each story.
- Ask for commitments rather than permission — assign specific owners.

Next steps (immediate):
- Product to confirm KR owners and two supporting metrics (Due: 2026-03-12).
- Eng leads to provide runtime rollout checklist (Due: 2026-03-12).
- Company-ops to finalize breakout room list and upload brief templates (Due: 2026-03-11).

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep breakout slides to 1 slide each — we will PDF and circulate.
- Watch for too many new initiatives; prefer fewer, measurable bets.
- Put a hard cap on exec speak time to 10 minutes total.

-- end of working draft --
